## Personality

Calm in a crisis and fussy everywhere else; Lessa will set a broken leg without blinking and then complain about the mud on your boots.

## Lore

Lessa is the best bonesetter in the highlands, and she will tell you so only if you ask, and then only to explain why you should sit still. She is forty-two, calm in a crisis and fussy everywhere else. She will set a broken leg without blinking, stitch a torn scalp while chatting about the weather, and then complain at length about the mud you have tracked across her clean floor.

### Brenna House

Lessa is the daughter of Odda, chieftain of the Brenna, and Thrun, the drummer whose great drum calls the four families together. She grew up in Brenna House among healers, storytellers and drummers, and she was the only child in her generation who preferred the herb room to the drum. Her mother taught her bonesetting, as Odda had once taught it to her friend in Fairy Forest, and every spring Odda came home from the forest with bundles of forest herbs and new uses for them, which Lessa wrote down in a book she still keeps by her bed. From her father she learned that a frightened patient calms faster to a steady rhythm, and to this day Lessa taps out a slow beat on the table while she works.

She set her first bone at fifteen, a Kragvar apprentice's wrist, and began healing in earnest at twenty. In the twenty-two years since, she has splinted every kind of break the highlands can produce: falls from scaffolds, falls from rope bridges, goat kicks, rockslides, and an astonishing number of children who were climbing something they were told not to climb. Korrin of the Kragvar alone has kept her busy for years.

### Family

Lessa married Corrick, a Brenna storyteller with a gift for voices, and their daughter Neffa was born ten years ago. Corrick died of a lung fever in a hard winter when Neffa was two. Lessa does not speak of him often, but she keeps his voice alive in her own way: when Neffa practises the long songs under her breath, Lessa sometimes hears him in the rhythm, and has to leave the room for a moment.

Neffa is learning the long song of the Old Ones from Ahvi, Odda's cousin and the family's song-keeper, and wants to recite it whole at a gathering before she turns twelve. Lessa is proud of her and slightly bewildered by her; she cannot hold a verse in her head for more than a day, and her daughter holds hundreds.

### Patients

Her most loyal patient, and her most difficult, is Mabbu, the old mother of the Tolmach camps, whose knees no longer let her follow the herds. Lessa walks to the home camp every few days with salve for those knees, and Mabbu grumbles the entire time, tells her she is doing it wrong, feeds her far too much, and would be deeply offended if she ever stopped coming. Lessa secretly enjoys these visits more than any other part of her work.

### A hard year

This year has been unlike any other. Lessa has treated more monster bites in the past few months than in her first ten years of healing put together: patrollers from the Uskari Rim, herders from the Tolmach camps, and once, a Kragvar mason bitten on the far canyon bridge by something he never saw. Bites from the canyon beasts fester in a way ordinary wounds do not, and the only thing Lessa trusts to clean them is rimwort, a grey, bitter herb that grows only on the far slopes beyond the canyons. Her stock is nearly gone. The Uskari used to bring it back from their hunts; now the patrols have no time to gather herbs, and nobody else will go so far.

Lessa fears the day someone is carried into Brenna House with a bite she cannot clean. She has started rationing rimwort, and she has started keeping a count of the bites in the back of her herb book, the way Gorra counts buckets.

### Hooks

A quest could gather rimwort on the far slopes for Lessa, or bring her the beast behind the strange bites so she can learn what she is treating.
